transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... we recently put in a brighter bathroom mirror at home, and ever since we did that, I just keep noticing my face. Specifically, the skin around my cheeks and my jaw. It looks uneven, or... I guess kind of saggy to me. It's been bothering me a lot, even though my husband says he can't really see what I'm talking about when I point it out to him.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your reflection throughout the day because of this concern?

Yeah, I do. Most mornings I end up checking my face from a few different angles in that new mirror, and I usually put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse just to try and cover it up. 

I don't know if I stare at mirrors all day long, but... I do notice that I compare my face to the other women I see at work. And I definitely try to avoid being in any casual pictures if I’m not feeling okay about how my skin looks that day.
Are you worried that this change in your skin is a sign of a serious underlying medical illness?

No, not really. I don't think I'm sick or anything like that. It's not a health worry... it's really just that I hate how it looks. I figure it's probably just my skin changing as I get older, but it just bothers me a lot to see it looking so uneven. So, no, I'm not worried about an illness.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out general hypochondriasis (F45.2) and primary OCD (F42); symptoms specifically fit Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22) characterized by preoccupation with perceived cosmetic flaws, mirror checking, and camouflage without illness anxiety.
